subject: Implementation

findings.subject: Implementation
findings.title: No integration/E2E tests exist; the DB-touching success path in TestingRepository is entirely untested

evidence.excerpt: var connection = CreateConnection(...); connection.Open(); var transaction = connection.BeginTransaction(); ... transaction.Commit();

findings.recommendation: All test projects contain only mocked unit tests (0% integration/E2E). The repository layer opens real SQL/Npgsql connections, begins transactions and commits/rolls back — none of this is exercised by any test; only the null-config, no-active-source and unsupported-type error branches are covered via mocks. Add a thin integration test layer (e.g. Testcontainers-backed SQL Server/PostgreSQL instance or a WebApplicationFactory-based test) that exercises the real ResetTestingAsync happy path and commit/rollback logic.

findings.subject: Implementation
findings.title: Coverage tool is referenced but never configured with a threshold or reported anywhere

evidence.excerpt: (directory is empty — no workflow runs dotnet test with coverage collection or reporting)

findings.recommendation: coverlet.collector is referenced in every test project but there is no .runsettings/coverage threshold, no coverage report generation step, and no CI to run it (workflows folder is empty). Add a coverage collection step (dotnet test --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage"), a minimum threshold, and publish/report the result in CI.

findings.subject: Implementation
findings.title: Placeholder test asserts nothing meaningful
findings.recommendation: PilotUtiltyApi.Domain.Tests contains only this scaffold-generated example test, which asserts nothing about real behavior and is the sole test in the Domain test project. Replace it with real tests for Domain classes (e.g. Models/Responses, Models/Dto) or remove it once real coverage exists.

findings.subject: Implementation
findings.title: No CI workflow runs the test suite on any change

evidence.excerpt: (directory is empty — no CI workflow file present)

findings.recommendation: Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs dotnet test (across all five test projects) on every push/PR, so regressions are caught automatically instead of relying on local runs only.

notes: Reviewed all 5 test projects (Domain, Repositories, Services, Shared, Web) plus TestingShared support project. Each test project apart from Shared.Tests contains exactly one narrowly-scoped test class (mirroring the 'Testing...' reset-data feature); this thinness is noted as context but is not separately scored since class/method-level coverage completeness isn't a review-testing checklist item (see review-maintainability/coding-standards for that angle).
